Some uses of the verb ‘to need'
We can use the verb ‘need’ with a passive infinitive or with an –ing verb when we want to express something that has to be done.
Developing software can be an arduous work as it needs a lot of planning, problems need to be fixed and customers' requirements need to be fulfilled.
1. We can use the verb ‘need’ with a passive infinitive when we want to express that a thing or person has to receive an action.

Example:
The performance of a company needs to be evaluated by the manager.
The structure we are going to use is the following:
Thing or person that receives the action + verb ‘need’ + to be + past participle of the main verb
Notice that we can either express the agent that is performing the action by using the preposition ‘by’, or we can omit the agent that performs the action if the context permits it.

2. Another way of expressing that something has to be done or that something or someone has to receive an action, is by using the verb ‘need’ with a gerund (verb in –ing). This structure will also have a passive sense.

Example:
The performance of the company needs evaluating.
The structure we use is the following:
Thing or person that receives the action + verb ‘need’ + main verb in –ing
When we use a gerund to express a passive sense, we do not mention the agent that performed the action.

Understanding the Concept of Performance Metrics
Performance metrics determines or describes the performance of an organization regarding specific processes.

Choosing the right performance metrics is important for evaluating the performance of a software development project and avoiding inefficiency in the processes. If the metrics are not chosen correctly, the organization could be evaluating the performance of processes that are not that relevant for the overall project. Besides, when paying too much attention to process that are not very important, the truly crucial ones could be left out. This can happen especially if the organization decides to use mainly the performance metrics that are easier to measure.

It’s important that an organization, whenever it assess the performance of a project, weights the effort to collect a metric against its value so that the collection of data does not become impractical.  

There are seven criteria that an organization should take into account when choosing what the most relevant performance metrics are: safety, time, cost, resources, scope, quality, and actions. Nevertheless, the organization must evaluate what metrics are most important in accordance to how the organization works and the nature of the project it is working on.

Finally, when choosing performance metrics, there are three important steps that can help discriminate what the most relevant measurements are:

1. Establish critical requirements.
2. Identify specific and quantifiable outputs of work (measurable results which can be used to determine the quality and performance of the product).
3. Establish targets that help measure results.

images.text: Developing software can be an arduous work as it needs a lot of planning, problems need to be fixed, and customers' requirements need to be fulfilled. That's why performance metrics need to be used by software organizations for easily spotting problems in the development processes throughout the development of a product. These metrics will help the manager and the team gather the information needed to address the issues and result in a better quality product.

Nevertheless, the performance metrics need evaluating before being used. An organization has to take into account the requirements of the customer, the quantifiable outputs of work, and the targets or goals of the projects in order to develop the appropriate performance metrics. Additionally, these metrics evolve depending on the state and the methodology an organization is following. For instance, before the Agile method, the defect tracking metric was one of the most relevant metrics, but once this new method was put forward, defect tracking was set aside as other metrics needed to be given more attention to. Furthermore, when an organization is still small, the metrics related to functional quality like customers' requirements and product design, among others, need to be regarded as paramount. But as the project grows complex, the structural quality metrics, which are related to efficiency or maintenance of software, for example, need more considering.

Some important performance metrics that companies find useful are: defect density, which measures the amount of bugs that were tracked on a given period of time; customer problems, that need to be measured by the customers' response to the problems in terms of both product defects and troubles in usability; and defect removal effectiveness, which needs calculating depending on the amount of defects that were removed in contrast with the defects that remain in the software.
